validity_contract: Docs under /opt/ibm/ILOG/CPLEX_Studio2211/doc/html/en-US/CPLEX/UsrMan/topics/progr_adv/. usr_cut_lazy_constr/02_defn.html: user cuts are "based on information already implied about the problem by the constraints; user cuts may not be strictly necessary to the problem, but they tighten the model." 04_diffs.html: cuts "can change the feasible space of the continuous relaxation but do not rule out any feasible integer solution that the rest of the model permits." Same page, consequence: "if valid and necessary constraints are mis-identified by the user and passed to CPLEX as user cuts, unpredictable and possibly incorrect results could occur." Dominance and symmetry: "Optimality-based cuts do not fit the definition of either a user cut nor a lazy constraint... However, CPLEX can support optimality-based cuts as lazy constraints." So removing non-optimal integer points is outside the contract; run: dominance cut y0<=0 reached 107.4 in 4 runs, one instance, no guarantee. Model: original (callbacks/presolveReduction.html: "performed by the user in the original model"). Including lazy constraints: no sentence says so, closest is "the rest of the model"; bendersatsp2.c uses cuts implied only by the lazy set, and Q11 reached the right optimum that way. Observed consequence of an invalid cut: silent wrong answer with a false proof (status=optimal value=106.4 dual=106.4 vs 107.4); a cut emptying the problem gives status=infeasible with err 0. Cuts do not bind incumbents: 04_diffs "it does not guarantee to check them at the time an integer-feasible solution candidate has been identified"; run: MIP start at the optimum, invalid cut added, result value=107.4 with the point violating the cut by 1.0.
treatment: Hint by contract in all modes. Doc callbackaddusercuts.html: "There is no guarantee CPLEX will use the constraints you specify... You can thus not assume that in subsequent callback invocations the relaxation solutions satisfy the constraints". FORCE "stays there", PURGE "can be purged later on", FILTER "can possibly not even add the cut". Multithreaded doc: anything passed in speculative tasks "might be discarded". Run, ATSP n=31, 3 seeds, 1 and 30 cuts/call, 1 thread, totals of 6 runs per mode (cuts added; re-added identical; later violated prev call/same node earlier/other nodes; checks; CPXgetnumcuts USER at end): global-force 270;0;0/0/0;9945;270. global-purge 260;2;0/7/2;6937;196. global-filter 264;2;0/7/2;7142;196. local-force 327;43;0/0/170;16565;196. local-purge 279;15;0/7/33;9266;138. local-filter 281;17;0/7/38;9472;134. FORCE's zero is one-thread, default RepeatPresolve only: RepeatPresolve=1 drops FORCE cuts (persistence), other threads see them late (threads). PURGE is real. FILTER is real at the root: valid objective-floor cut on 100 columns, violation 0.2: filter 5/5 later root points violate it, numcuts 0; purge and force 0/6, numcuts 1; same on all four releases. In the tree FILTER behaved like PURGE on my instances (8721 tiny cuts accepted at one node, numcuts 1560 on another run). Limits: EACHCUTLIM=0 no effect on callback cuts (9 nodes vs 34583 no-cut baseline at that setting); CUTSFACTOR=1.0 cuts still act (7 nodes, no no-cut baseline at that setting); CUTPASS=N caps root rounds at N (1, 3, 5 measured), -1 removes the root call; Community's 1000-row cap does not count cuts (numcuts 12501). Ignoring this restriction will lead to incorrect solutions." Lazy constraints are not mentioned. [forum] Ruthmair, staff (forum_lazy.txt:49): "The recommended way is to add all cuts that might cut off integer solutions via cbLazy(), even during a user cut callback". Consequence [run]: y0>=1 removing the optimum gives status=optimal value=97.4 of 107.4; an impossible objective cut gives infeasible; incumbents are not vetted (optimum as MIP start plus a cut removing it: optimal 107.4, returned point violates the cut by 1). Dominance [run]: removing non-optimal points is outside the contract and produced wrong answers. Parallel columns with b1+b2=4, cut b1<=1, (1,3) still optimal, 5 of 5 seeds where the cut was non-trivial (the other 5 had k=6, no power): PreCrush=1 gives status=optimal 17351/17487, 16694/16749, 17465/17666, 18173/18247, 15513/15579, and with Heuristics=0 status=infeasible on all five. Same on 11.0.3 and 13.0.2 for seeds 1 and 4. PreCrush=0 keeps the value only because the cut is ignored. DualReductions=0, LazyConstraints=1 and cblazy kept the value, with the cut obeyed where it was added (on seed 3 it was never added under those settings). Not every dominance cut fails: b1<=b2 kept the value on all seeds run, and y0<=0 kept it with presolve off.
treatment: Hint, not binding. No force flag. [forum] Ruthmair: "cuts added by cbCut() might be discarded if they do not meet the solver's conditions (numerics, density, etc.)". [forum] Clement, staff (forum_filter.txt:48): "Note that even if the cut is not filtered out, it is not necessarily applied. The solver will maintain a pool of potential cuts and apply (or even remove ones that have been applied) as it sees fit." [run] native_error=0 in every case below, baseline S0 1050 nodes: +1e7 on an unused column: not obeyed, 461/787, 1050 nodes. +1e-4 on 20000 unused columns: 472/787, 1050 nodes. Violation 1e-7 or below: no effect; 1e-6 applied. 2000 cuts at one call: 1432 still violated next call, then 1046. Same cut found again: 598 of 996 cuts at ATSP n=120; 17135 of 70682 on a knapsack with covers. Earlier cuts violated later: 2645 at n=120 (365 of 878 calls, max 205 at one call). The hook cannot separate purged from in-pool-but-not-in-this-LP. cblazy from MIPNODE is the binding alternative and needs LazyConstraints=1: dense cut obeyed (2/403, the root repeats, 539 nodes), all 2000 obeyed from the first tree node. scope_default_meaning:
Chosen PER CUT by the `local` argument of the row's creation call (SCIPcreateEmptyRowSepa); SCIPaddRow itself has no scope.

local=TRUE: the row stays in the subtree of the node where it was added. It never left it in any run (optimum kept under 3 node selections, 3 releases). Exception, executed: at depth 0 SCIP rewrites it to global (SCIProwIsLocal 1 before SCIPaddRow, 0 after; sepastore.c:459).

local=FALSE: a CLAIM OF GLOBAL VALIDITY, not "installed everywhere". The row enters the node's LP and stays inside that subtree through the fork. It moves to the next focused node outside the subtree only if still at age 0 (non-zero dual in the last LP), solve.c:1332 "keep all active global cuts that where applied in the previous node in the lp", `if( !lp->rows[i]->local && lp->rows[i]->age == 0 )`; age lp.c:15285. Same code at solve.c:1445 in 10.0.2. Otherwise it is absent from nodes outside the subtree unless it is also in the global pool.

So it is neither local nor global in force, and S1 under default selection reads "local in force" only by luck of the age. Executed, s1age 9.2.1:
- selection=default local=false: value=107.4 KEPT, last subtree call age=1, first sibling call in LP=false violation=21.7

- "Cutting planes that do not violate the current LP relaxation solution are discarded by COPT." (11259)

treatment:
A hint, not binding, and there is no force flag. Executed.
- Not binding: at default settings on the ATSP a cut added after 21 nodes ended with value=549 and "final solution violates it by 1.000". Under TreeCutLevel=1, incumbents=3 violating=2.
- Silent filter with rc=0: on y3+0.01 za3 (norm about 1), violation 1e-3 is accepted (fires again on the node, later violations 0/152), and 1e-4 is dropped (no re-fire, later 152/152, path identical to no cut). On a dense objective floor (norm about 1800), raw 0.1 is dropped and raw 1.0 accepted. So the rule is not raw violation; a threshold between 1e-4 and 5.6e-4 on normalised violation fits both, which is my inference.
- Selection in a round: ATSP n=40, 7 cuts at once: 4/7 hold at the next call, 7/7 at the one after.
- Purge: ATSP n=40, 3 root cuts, 3200 nodes: 40 of 3450 later calls had one violated, and 3/3 cuts were violated at some point. A root cut can leave the LP later.
- One-term cuts: silently dropped in the tree, honoured at the root (Q10).

validity_contract: There is no prose contract: this is my reading of headers and source. Pages read: the user guide TOC (https://www.coin-or.org/Cbc/) and its 'Getting Good Bounds' page (https://www.coin-or.org/Cbc/heuristics) have nothing on cut validity; ./branching and ./advanced were not read. Closest wording: CglCutGenerator.hpp: 'Generate cuts for the model data contained in si.' CbcCountRowCut.hpp:69-71: 'For locally valid cuts, the node will be the search tree node where the cut was generated. For globally valid cuts, it's the node where the cut was activated.' Cbc_C_Interface.h:164-167 (master): 'if pre-processing is on then the number of variables and constraints in this problem will be smaller than the dimensions of the initial problem'. CbcModel.cpp 2.10.12:13307: 'Only global cuts are useful' at a new solution, and :13345 'set to run on new solution but NOT globally valid!!'. So validity is relative to the model handed to the hook. Observed consequences of an invalid cut: at the root on integer columns, silent wrong optimum with status=optimal and a matching dual (108.4 vs 109.4). On continuous columns only, the returned point violates it and the value is the true optimum (S1z-root, za3+zb3<=4). Below the root, plain, only the subtree is affected. Dominance or cutoff cuts: nothing forbids or checks them, and S1i removed integer points from a subtree and still returned the optimum. But Cbc fixes columns before the search even with preprocess and presolve off (hook reads [1,1] on rewards in a redundant row, [0,0] on a rowless dummy), and a cut contradicting that fixing gave status=infeasible on a feasible model (out_cbc_bounds_*.txt).
